text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Detected p99 latency spike on dedicated pool 'redwood-dedicated-prod-07' starting ~1767778880. Autoscaler handshake latency increased, warmup failures observed. Queue depth > 600 for 3m. Streaming stalls reported by multiple customers. Paging on-call.

Alice Nguyen: I'm on it. Paging infra and runtime. Which route is most affected?

oncall-pager: PagerDuty: Incident PD-82431 triggered for 'dedicated-pool-handshake-latency'. Primary on-call: Alice Nguyen.

Ben Ortiz: Logs show handshakes were timing out to the node-provisioner at ~1767778840-1767778870. Error snippet: `handshake_timeout: exceeded 20s waiting for slot` and `warmup 0/4 succeeded`.

Carla Chen: Customer-facing routes impacted: /v1/generate (streaming), /v1/chat/stream. Non-streaming batch endpoints degraded but still returning with high tail latency.

Dave K: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) Route heavy streaming traffic to fallback model variant (cpu-optimized or small bf16) 2) Increase handshake timeout temporarily 3) Manually spin up a warm pool node via admin console. Which is fastest?

Alice Nguyen: Do 1 and 3 in parallel. Ben, can you open the manual warmup and confirm node health? Carla, prepare an outbound message for affected customers (short blurb). Emily, start an eval run to check quality of fallback model for top 10 prompts.

Ben Ortiz: Manual warmup started: `adminctl warmup --pool redwood-dedicated-prod-07 --count 3 --profile warm`  (console task id: warmup-1767778892). K8s pods starting: rdp-07-node-31 -> Pending -> Running.

infra-bot: Node rdp-07-node-31 moved to Running at 1767778898. KV-cache priming 0%. Warmup logs: `loading weights`, `compiling kernels`, `priming kv-cache`.

Carla Chen: Draft to customers: "We're experiencing elevated streaming latency affecting some requests. We're actively scaling and routing traffic to lower-latency fallbacks. No data loss. Updates every 15 minutes." Thoughts?

Alice Nguyen: Good. Send now from status page and DM account owners for top 5 customers.

Ben Ortiz: Handshake error rate graph: last minute: 42% handshake failures. After warmup-1767778892, handshake failures dropped to 18% but queue depth still at ~320.

Dave K: Apply quick fallback routing: add policy to route streaming requests >10s expected tokens to model variant redwood-bert-small-stream. Command: `routectl add-policy --selector 'streaming=true and expected_tokens>100' --target redwood-bert-small-stream --priority 80`.

Alice Nguyen: Execute now.

Ben Ortiz: Policy applied. Live metrics: streaming P95 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.8s for routed traffic. Overall p99 still at 6.8s due to tail streaming stalls.

Emily Forrest: Running quick evaluation on fallback variant — initial 100 samples show ~5% difference in top-k on intents that use knowledge retrieval. Acceptable as emergency fallback.

infra-bot: Autoscaler logs: `scale_attempt(1767778850): insufficient warm slots, fallback to queued requests`. Autoscaler backoff timer shows 2 retries with exponential backoff; handshake time drift observed between control plane and node agent (clock skew ~2.1s).

Alice Nguyen: Clock skew — could that affect handshake timeouts?

Ben Ortiz: Yes, some agents time out if control-plane timestamp >> agent. Quick fix: bump handshake timeout from 20s -> 40s via runtime flag to prevent premature aborts while warmup completes. Setting now on pool redwood-dedicated-prod-07.

Dave K: Flag set. `runtimectl set --pool redwood-dedicated-prod-07 --handshake-timeout 40s` returning ok.

Carla Chen: Customer update posted. Account owners pinged.

Alice Nguyen: Are we seeing any downstream retries or billing anomalies due to fallback? Need to track.

Ben Ortiz: Note: some streaming clients retry aggressively leading to more queue amplification. I suggest enabling transient 429 with Retry-After on routes we control to throttle client retries.

Dave K: Implemented 429 policy for high-queue routes: `routectl set --selector 'queue_depth>200' --status 429 --retry-after 10`.

Alice Nguyen: Good. Monitor for 15m. Also open a customer-impact tally: which customers saw >10% error increase? Carla?

Carla Chen: Early list: AcmeHealth (streams degraded), Searchly (p99 up 400ms), EduLabs (saw reconnects). I'll add full list to the incident doc.

infra-bot: warmup-1767778892 completed: 3 nodes warm, KV-cache primed ~58% at 1767778940. Queue depth decreased to 120.

Ben Ortiz: After manual warmup and fallback routing we see p95 stable at 600ms, p99 at 1.2s, streaming stalls reduced from 24 incidents/min -> 2 incidents/min.

Alice Nguyen: Triage summary for paging: Root cause appears to be combined: burst of streaming traffic + autoscaler warmup delay (handshake timeouts and clock skew) causing queue amplification and client-side retries. Mitigations that helped: manual warmup, fallback routing to smaller model, increased handshake timeout, 429 throttling.

Emily Forrest: Follow-ups: 1) Autoscaler should consider transient warmup quota to pre-warm a small buffer for hot pools 2) Add clock-sync healthcheck for node agents 3) Improve client retry guidance in streaming docs to avoid thundering retries.

Dave K: I'll open two tickets: INF-1129 (pre-warm buffer policy) and INF-1130 (agent clock sync probe).

Carla Chen: I'll prepare a short postmortem and customer-impact timeline. Include per-customer latency deltas and mitigation times.

Alice Nguyen: Great. We'll keep monitoring for next 30m. If p99 rises above 2s, escalate to SRE lead. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

oncall-pager: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident closed to page after 30m stable metrics.

Alice Nguyen: Marking this thread for postmortem. Adding owners: Ben (runtime), Dave (autoscaler infra), Carla (customer comms), Emily (eval + docs).

Ben Ortiz: Leaving final note - logs attached to incident: `s3://incidents/1767778888/handshake-logs.tar.gz`.

Carla Chen: Postmortem ETA: 48h.

Alice Nguyen: End of thread — transitioning to incident doc.
